questions.prompt: Which sentence uses quotation marks and punctuation correctly?

options.text: Mia said "The ferry leaves at noon."
Mia said, "The ferry leaves at noon".
Mia said, "The ferry leaves at noon."
Mia said, "The ferry leaves at noon.

questions.explanation: Direct speech introduced by 'said' takes a comma before the opening quotation mark, and the full stop belongs inside the closing quotation mark.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses correct subject-verb agreement?

options.text: The stack of wet towels is beside the door.
The stack of wet towels are beside the door.
The stack of wet towels were beside the door.
The stack of wet towels have been beside the door.

questions.explanation: The singular subject 'stack' requires the singular verb 'is'; the nearby plural noun 'towels' does not control verb agreement.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct pronoun?

options.text: The guide handed the spare map to Mila and I.
The guide handed the spare map to Mila and she.
The guide handed the spare map to Mila and we.
The guide handed the spare map to Mila and me.

questions.explanation: The preposition 'to' requires an object pronoun, so 'me' is correct; 'I', 'she' and 'we' are subject pronouns.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct verb tense to show that one action was completed before another past action?

options.text: By the time the bell rang, the students have finished their posters.
By the time the bell rang, the students had finished their posters.
By the time the bell rang, the students will finish their posters.
By the time the bell rang, the students finish their posters.

questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had finished' identifies an action completed before the past event 'the bell rang'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the paired conjunction correctly?

options.text: Neither the trumpet nor the flute was ready for the concert.
Neither the trumpet or the flute was ready for the concert.
Neither the trumpet and the flute was ready for the concert.
Neither the trumpet but the flute was ready for the concert.

questions.explanation: The negative paired conjunction is 'neither ... nor'; 'or', 'and' and 'but' cannot replace 'nor' in this construction.

questions.prompt: Which option correctly joins the ideas into one complete complex sentence?

options.text: Because the path was flooded, so we took the longer route.
Because the path was flooded. We took the longer route.
Because the path was flooded, we took the longer route.
Because the path was flooded, and we took the longer route.

questions.explanation: The dependent clause beginning with 'Because' must connect to an independent clause; a comma correctly separates them without an unnecessary conjunction.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly shows that the tools belong to all four gardeners?

options.text: The four gardener's tools were beside the gate.
The four gardeners' tools were beside the gate.
The four gardeners tools were beside the gate.
The four gardeners's tools were beside the gate.

questions.explanation: For a regular plural noun ending in s, the possessive apostrophe follows the final s; 'gardeners'' shows ownership by multiple gardeners.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?

options.text: Only one of the carved signs stand beside the entrance.
Only one of the carved signs were standing beside the entrance.
Only one of the carved signs have stood beside the entrance.
Only one of the carved signs stands beside the entrance.

questions.explanation: The subject is the singular expression 'Only one', requiring 'stands'; the plural noun 'signs' belongs to the phrase 'of the carved signs'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses punctuation to introduce a list?

options.text: The kit included three items; a torch, a whistle and a map.
The kit included three items. A torch, a whistle and a map.
The kit included three items: a torch, a whistle and a map.
The kit included three items a torch, a whistle and a map.

questions.explanation: A colon correctly introduces a list after the complete clause 'The kit included three items'; a semicolon or full stop would incorrectly separate the list, while omitting punctuation leaves the introduction unclear.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a possessive relative pronoun?

options.text: The student whose scarf was missing checked the lost property box.
The student who's scarf was missing checked the lost property box.
The student who scarf was missing checked the lost property box.
The student whom scarf was missing checked the lost property box.

questions.explanation: 'Whose' is the possessive relative pronoun showing that the scarf belongs to the student; 'who's' is a contraction, while 'who' and 'whom' do not express possession.
